plan: This is a second-price auction with 3 bidders and independent private values uniform on [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy: since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) when you win, there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding exactly your value ensures you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids, capturing all positive-profit opportunities, and never risks paying more than your value.

This is a second-price auction with independent private values uniformly distributed on [0,49]. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win, bidding your value ensures you win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and avoid losses otherwise. There's no incentive to shade the bid. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid exactly my value of $23.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others bid. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value ensures I never overpay and always capture positive profit when I have the highest valuation. Bidding above value risks negative profit; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $36.
